wasteNot.title: Waste Not!
wasteNot.description:
Waste Not is an environmental initiative designed to educate local residents on the importance of reusing household items rather than discarding them in their neighbourhoods.

The campaign encourages residents to share reusable items through local networks or donate them to charities.

Browse our Locations in the menu to discover donation opportunities near you and help keep items in use for a more sustainable community.

about.title: About
about.description: The UK discards 640,000 tonnes of reusable items each year. Kind Cycle, a group of residents focused on sustainability, is tackling this issue with projects that reduce waste and connect communities by promoting reuse over recycling. With expertise in architecture, design, and events, they create initiatives that educate and build stronger communities.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.description: Want to learn more about the Kind Cycle and Waste Not project? Want to suggest a charity or an organisation to include? Pop us a message!

ferrylane.name: Ferry Lane Estate
ferrylane.description: Ferry Lane Estate is the first delivery location for the Waste Not campaign. Bold, eye-catching information panels promoting household item donations have been strategically installed in common dumping areas across the estate. Explore our comprehensive guide on where and how to donate.

haringey.name: Haringey
haringey.description: Donating is easier than discarding. Haringey residents can explore a comprehensive list of charities and organisations offering free collections and drop-offs for clothes, furniture, appliances, and more. Simply click on a section, choose an organisation, see how it works, and donate.

broadwaterfarm.name: Broadwater Farm
broadwaterfarm.description: Broadwater Farm residents can easily find local charities and organisations offering free collection and drop-off services for clothes, furniture, appliances, and more. Simply explore the sections below, choose an organisation, see how it works, and make your donation. The delivery of the Waste Not project at Broadwater Farm has been funded by the Haringey Community Carbon Fund.

babyItems.name: Baby Items
babyItems.description: Babies grow quickly, and outgrown items take up space. Donate gently used baby gear to families in need and free up room.

clothes.name: Clothes
clothes.description: Clear out your closet and donate what you no longer wear. Give your shoes and clothes a second life and let someone else enjoy them.

furniture.name: Furniture
furniture.description: If furniture you no longer need or love is taking up space, donate it and make someone's day – they'll even pick it up from your doorstep!

repair.name: Repair It!
repair.description: Fixing broken items is an easy way to reduce waste while saving the planet and your wallet.

household.name: Household Goods
household.description: What you don't need, someone else will love. The household items you no longer want might be exactly what someone else is looking for!

ferrylane.description:
Sharing what you no longer need with your Ferry Lane neighbours: they're local and can pick up items with ease. From small items no one would travel for to large items that would require costly transport, it's all easier when your neighbours are nearby. You can even donate food your cat doesn't like, fridge surplus before going on holiday, or extra pantry items.

Click or scan the QR code below to join the FLAG WhatsApp community and post your items there.

whatsApp.label: Join the FLAG WhatsApp community link

haringey.description: Sharing with neighbours is a great way to keep good things in use and build connections. Because they’re close by, neighbours can pick things up easily — whether it’s a small item that isn’t worth a trip or a larger one that would cost money to transport. You can even share pet food your cat won’t eat, fridge leftovers before a holiday, or extra pantry items. Just post in your local WhatsApp or Facebook group, or mention it to someone nearby — you might make a neighbour’s day!

broadwaterfarm.description: Sharing with neighbours is a great way to keep good things in use and build connections. Because they’re close by, neighbours can pick things up easily — whether it’s a small item that isn’t worth a trip or a larger one that would cost money to transport. You can even share pet food your cat won’t eat, fridge leftovers before a holiday, or extra pantry items. Just post in your local WhatsApp or Facebook group, or mention it to someone nearby — you might make a neighbour’s day!

lloydPark.name: Lloyd Park Children's Charity
lloydPark.about: Lloyd Park Children's Charity provides vital services and support for children and families in the Waltham Forest community.
lloydPark.howItWorks: Their Baby Bank project offers essentials like baby clothes, equipment, and toiletries to families in need. They collect items for children aged 0-5. For up to date list of items accepted, drop-off locations and times, check out the website and send an email.

pramDepot.name: Pram Depot
pramDepot.about: PramDepot is an arts-led recycling project that supports vulnerable new mums by providing recycled baby clothes and equipment.
pramDepot.howItWorks: Gently used baby gear can be donated at the Wood Green location. A list of accepted items is available on the website. To arrange a drop-off, simply schedule a time using the online donation form.

olio.name: Olio
olio.about: Olio is a mobile app that connects communities to share items for free, helping reduce household and food waste.
olio.howItWorks: Download the app and create an account. Once registered, you can post items you want to give away, such as food, household goods. You can also browse listings from others in your local area to request or borrow items. Users communicate directly through the app to arrange pick-up or collection.

freecycle.name: Freecycle
freecycle.about: Freecycle is a platform where people give away items they no longer need for free, promoting reuse and reducing waste.
freecycle.howItWorks: Sign up, create an account, and join your borough group and nearby ones. You can post listings of items you want to give away, such as furniture, electronics, or clothes, and arrange collection through direct messages. Freecycle promotes community-driven exchanges with no financial transactions. Users can also post wanted ads for specific items.

facebookMarketplace.name: Facebook Marketplace
facebookMarketplace.about: Facebook Marketplace is an online platform where users can buy, sell, and give away items within their local community.
facebookMarketplace.howItWorks: To donate items on Facebook Marketplace, log into Facebook and go to the Marketplace sections. Click "Create New Listing", select "Item for Sale", and set the price to £0. Add photos, descriptions, location and item details. Local users can message you directly to arrange collection.

britishHeartFoundation.name: British Heart Foundation
britishHeartFoundation.about: The British Heart Foundation is a charity dedicated to funding research into heart disease and supporting those affected by cardiovascular conditions.
britishHeartFoundation.howItWorks: The British Heart Foundation accepts donations of clothing, books, electrical goods, and furniture. They offer free collection for larger items, which you can arrange through an online form. Just provide the item details, preferred collection date, address, and contact info.

encouragingReuse.name: Encouraging Reuse
encouragingReuse.howItWorks: The "Encouraging Reuse" shop is a community-focused space dedicated to promoting sustainability through the donation and reuse of items.

traid.name: TRAID
traid.about: TRAID is a UK charity focused on reducing textile waste by turning unwanted clothes into resources for global development projects.
traid.howItWorks: Donated clothing are collect and resold to fund their initiatives. You can donate clean, wearable clothes by dropping them off at TRAID donation banks or their charity shops. For larger donations, TRAID offers a free home collection service, which can be arranged through their website.

weCollectWeDonate.name: WeCollectWeDonate
weCollectWeDonate.about: WeCollectWeDonate is a social enterprise that collects unwanted items such as clothes, books, and home goods directly from your doorstep, free of charge.
weCollectWeDonate.howItWorks: They resell or donate these items to charities, helping raise funds for causes like homelessness, mental health, and education. You can arrange a collection easily through their website, where they accept items in good, reusable condition.

haringeyFixers.name: Haringey Fixers
haringeyFixers.about: Haringey Fixers is a community-led charity promoting repair and reuse.They offer monthly Repair Cafés, where local residents can bring items to repair, helping reduce waste and teach repair skills.
haringeyFixers.howItWorks: A Repair Café is a community event where locals fix household items and reduce waste. Volunteers help repair things like appliances, furniture, and clothing. Held several weekends a month in Haringey, these free sessions aim to promote sustainability. Check the calendar for upcoming events and book a free weekend slot.

northLondonWasteAuthority.name: North London Waste Authority
northLondonWasteAuthority.about: The North London Waste Authority (NLWA) manages waste disposal and recycling services for seven north London boroughs, and delivers multiple projects aiming to reduce waste and improve sustainability.
northLondonWasteAuthority.howItWorks: NLWA promotes repair initiatives to reduce waste, offering a repair directory on their website. This directory includes resources like repair services, DIY repair tips, and guides to extend the life of household items.

clothesBanks.name: Clothes Banks
clothesBanks.about: Several charities, including TRAID and The Salvation Army, have clothes banks located throughout the city, where you can drop off unwanted clothes, textiles, and shoes at any time.
clothesBanks.howItWorks: Simply bag your items and place them in the designated recycling bins. These banks are conveniently located in multiple spots. Here's a map to help you find the nearest one.

footprintForGood.name: Footprint for Good
footprintForGood.about: Footprint for Good supports at-risk young people: through the Repair Restore Respect program, participants learn upcycling and restoration by repairing donated furniture — building confidence, practical skills, and promoting sustainability.
footprintForGood.howItWorks: You can request a free furniture collection using our online form. The team will contact you within 5 working days to confirm the date. This service is currently for furniture items only. They accept sofas, wardrobes, bed frames, tables, chairs, shelving and storage solutions.

prayHaringey.name: Children's Storehouse from Pray Haringey
prayHaringey.about: Pray Haringey is a faith-based, community-focused network in Haringey. One of their initiatives, Children’s Storehouse, collects good-quality donations for children aged 0–7 and distributes them to local families in need.
prayHaringey.howItWorks: Donations can be dropped off, or collections can be arranged. They accept cots and cot bedding, high chairs, prams or buggies, safety gates, clothes, toys, and books suitable for children aged 0–7.

communityClothingCollection.name: Community Clothing Collection
communityClothingCollection.about: Community Clothing Collection is a company based in London that operates a free home collection service for clothing donations in London and Essex
communityClothingCollection.howItWorks: Pick a charity you want to support and book a free collection online. They’ll collect your unwanted clothes and accessories from your doorstep and deliver them to your chosen cause. Just check the list of accepted items before you donate.

collectMyClothes.name: Collect My Clothes
collectMyClothes.about: Collect My Clothes is a UK-wide, free home collection service that recycles your clothing, footwear, bags, and accessories to raise money for partner charities.
collectMyClothes.howItWorks: Bag up your clean, reusable unwanted item, request a free collection online and choose a charity to support. The items are ethically recycled and your chosen charity receives £200–£250 per ton collected.

redonate.name: reDONATE.uk
redonate.about: reDONATE.uk is a charity that gives unwanted clothing a second life by reducing waste and supporting communities.
redonate.howItWorks: Book a free collection online, and the team will pick up your unwanted clothes from your doorstep. reDONATE accepts good-quality clothing, shoes, accessories, jewellery, perfumes, and more. They also take small bric-a-brac and books if you include them with a clothing donation.

collectNDonate.name: Collect ’N Donate
collectNDonate.about: Collect ’N Donate is a UK-based charity collection service.They offer free doorstep pickup of good-quality items and collaborate with a variety of local charities to redistribute them for community benefit
collectNDonate.howItWorks: Book a free clothes collection online or by phone. Place your items in a labeled bag or box and leave them outside at the arranged time. Their team will collect them from your doorstep. You can donate adult and children’s clothing, paired shoes, accessories, bags, belts, jewellery, books, CDs/DVDs, and other bric-a-brac.

help2Collect.name: Help 2 Collect
help2Collect.about: Help 2 Collect is a UK-based donation service that offers free collection of quality items to support charities. It has raised over £53,000 and diverted thousands of tonnes of clothing from landfill.
help2Collect.howItWorks: Book a free home collection online or by phone, and the team will pick up your donations—such as clothes, shoes, bags, belts, baby itmes and soft toys—directly from your doorstep.

iCollectClothes.name: iCollectClothes
iCollectClothes.about: iCollectClothes is a UK-based service that facilitates free doorstep collections of unwanted clothing, supporting various charities through the resale of donated items.
iCollectClothes.howItWorks: To donate, simply visit the iCollectClothes website, choose your preferred charity, then schedule a convenient free doorstep collection. You can include items such as clothes, shoes, and accessories.

sueRyder.name: Sue Ryder
sueRyder.about: Sue Ryder is a UK charity that provides expert palliative care and bereavement support, helping people at the end of life and those coping with loss. Funds raised through their charity shops support hospice and neurological care across the country
sueRyder.howItWorks: They offer a free furniture collection service, which can be booked online or by calling their National Furniture Line (0333 003 1883). They collect good-quality sofas, tables, wardrobes, beds, and small electrical items with fire safety labels where required.

jacksSofaDrops.name: Jacks Sofa Drops
jacksSofaDrops.about: Jacks Sofa Drops is trusted across London and Surrey for reliable, eco-friendly sofa removals and furniture collection. Reusable items are donated to local charities or rehomed, and anything beyond repair is responsibly recycled to keep it out of landfill.
jacksSofaDrops.howItWorks: Book a collection using their online form, and the team will respond within 24 hours to confirm a convenient pickup time. They offer free collection for gently used sofas, sectionals, and dining tables with minor wear — including light stains or pet hair.

freegle.name: Freegle
freegle.about: Freegle is a UK-based community platform that enables people to give away and receive items for free, promoting reuse and reducing waste.
freegle.howItWorks: To donate, join your local Freegle group online, post a description of the item you want to give away, and arrange collection with an interested member.

loveJunk.name: LoveJunk
loveJunk.about: LoveJunk is a marketplace that connects users with licensed waste collectors and junk reusers for secure, cost-effective, and eco-friendly rubbish and bulky item removal.
loveJunk.howItWorks: Users can post a job on LoveJunk for free by uploading photos and a brief description of their items. Nearby licensed waste collectors and reuse organisations can then view the listing, submit quotes, or offer to collect reusable items at no charge.
